cur-fossil-okladnikov.dateNote: In 2007 Johannes Krause and Svante Pääbo's team read DNA from bones found in this cave in the Altai Mountains, Siberia. They were Neanderthal, so Neanderthals had lived about 2,000 km further east than was thought. The bones are Late Ice Age, under 0.05 million years old.
cur-fossil-okladnikov.summary: A Siberian cave whose bones showed Neanderthals lived far into Asia.

cur-fossil-denisova.dateNote: In 2008 a child's finger bone was dug from this cave in Siberia's Altai Mountains. Its DNA, read in 2010, revealed a lost kind of human: the Denisovans. The bone is about 76,000–52,000 years old (under 0.1 million years). In 2026 ancient proteins showed that fossils from Xujiayao, in northern China, were Denisovan too. Also in 2026, teeth, skull pieces and the first known Denisovan forearm bone were reported from Bianfu Cave in Yunnan, south-west China, about 167,000-134,000 years old.

cur-find-chagyrskaya.dateNote: DNA from Neanderthals in this cave in Russia's Altai Mountains, about 54,000 years old, included a father and his teenage daughter: the first known Neanderthal family (Skov et al., Nature, 2022).
